description: We are 3 CS new grads with no experience with NASA data, but interested in learning through this challenge and coming up with novel ways to use SAR data.
summary: AI data centers are announced as single numbers, a gigawatt or ten billion dollars, years before they are built and before anyone sees what they will mean for the land and the small town water systems they depend on. We built an interactive map that uses satellite radar to close that gap. Sentinel-1 radar measured 8,462 acres changed at 29 finished campuses since 2017, 6,888 of them not built on before. NASA-ISRO's new NISAR radar, which sees through cloud every 12 days, shows 602 acres getting much brighter, the signature of new buildings and steel, at 3 Stargate campuses still under construction, months ahead of the newest aerial photos. We linked each campus to its water utility and river, lake or aquifer, checked those sources with SWOT, OPERA DISP-S1 and NISAR, and turned announced investments into land and water: by 2035 the 46 campuses studied would use as much water as about 1.0 million people use in a year (range 193,000 to 1.8 million), and, if built as announced, 5 small utilities would need to supply more water to linked campuses than to all their customers today.
details:
Deserto is a four-chapter story map of 54 US data center campuses and the 25 water sources they are linked to. 1) Land: for 29 finished campuses, Sentinel-1 radar (ESA) shows the month each patch of ground changed since 2017; press Play to watch campuses grow as dated aerial photos swap in. Of the 8,462 acres that changed, the pre-construction NLCD land-cover map shows 2,578 acres of farmland, 2,648 of shrubland and grassland and 828 of forest. 2) NISAR now: we read every NISAR image of the 3 campuses it covers since June 2026 and mapped ground more than 3 dB brighter: 315 acres at Vantage Frontier (Texas), 286 at Project Jupiter (New Mexico) and 1 at Lordstown (Ohio), which is going inside an existing factory. 3) Water: each campus is linked through EPA records to its utility and named source. SWOT tracks river and lake levels; OPERA DISP-S1 (2016-2026) and NISAR interferograms (2026) track ground sinking over 8 aquifers. 4) 2035: announced megawatts and dollars become land and water, in low, middle and high scenarios, using rates measured at the built campuses: 28,598 acres and as much water as about 1.0 million people use in a year.

How it works: radar change detection against a 12-month baseline (F1), then per-MW rates for land, cost and water (F2-F4), the campus's share of its utility's supply (F5), and a build ramp to 2035 (F8). Every number traces to a CSV with a source link, and every judgment call is logged in DECISIONS.md. The map says "linked to", never "caused by".

Why it matters: residents and water boards can check from space, every 12 days, whether announced money is turning into buildings, and see which water source a campus would depend on before it is built.

Built with Python (pandas, xarray, rasterio, geopandas, earthaccess, asf_search), JavaScript with MapLibre GL, and free NASA, ESA, EPA and USGS data.
